Shock as Live World War II-Era Grenades Sold at Texas Estate Sale: 'Not Your Typical Estate Sale Find'

Texas police this week jumped into action after someone purchased what turned out to be live World War II-era grenades at an estate sale.
The post Shock as Live World War II-Era Grenades Sold at Texas Estate Sale: ‘Not Your Typical Estate Sale Find’ appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
Texas police this week jumped into action after someone purchased what turned out to be live World War II-era grenades at an estate sale.

The Austin Police Association this week posted a photo of the World War II-era grenades and police response. According to authorities, a resident bought some boxes at an estate sale, only to find the grenades in the box. The Austin Police Association’s bomb squad addressed the situation and confirmed that the grenades were, in fact “live and active.”

“Huge thanks to our patrol officers, who quickly secured the scene, set up a perimeter, and kept neighbors safe while they waited for EOD [explosive ordnance disposal],” the Austin Police Association wrote on social media.

“And a big shoutout to our APD [Austin Police Department] Bomb Squad. These officers bring a level of training, expertise, and steady nerves that most people never see. Handling 80-year-old explosives with unknown stability is dangerous, precise work, and they do it with the professionalism this city counts on. The devices were safely seized and removed,” the post continued, emphasizing that there was no crime here.

“If you ever come across old military ordnance (grenades, shells, mortar rounds, etc.), even if you think it’s inert, don’t touch it, don’t move it, and call 911. Let the experts handle it,” they added. “Proud of the men and women who answered this call. ”

In total, authorities found six grenades.

“Bomb Squad personnel assessed the devices, including X-ray examination,” a public information officer with the Austin Police Department told the Houston Chronicle. “Based on their interpretation of the X-ray images, the grenades appeared to be live and were treated accordingly.”

“Bomb Squad personnel subsequently conducted render-safe procedures to eliminate any potential hazards,” the individual added.

This is hardly the first case of individuals unexpectedly stumbling upon dangerous items. Last year, police responded to a Goodwill in Palatka, Florida, after employees spotted a live grenade in one of the donation bins. The grenade was never placed in the retail store, and the St. Johns County Sheriff’s Office Bomb Squad removed and detonated it.

“We want to remind the community to thoroughly check all items before donating, ensuring that hazardous items, such as explosives, firearms or ammunition, are not accidentally included,” the Palatka Police Department said in a statement after the incident.

Topic:Track Cycling

Australia won silver in the men's sprint at the World Championships in Shanghai. (Reuters: Kacper Pempel)

Australia finished with the silver medal in the men's team sprint at the UCI Track Cycling World Championships.

The Netherlands won the gold.

The Australians had defeated a British line-up missing Matt Richardson in the first round.

Australia has claimed a silver medal in the men's team sprint on the opening night of the UCI Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai.

The Australian trio of Leigh Hoffman, Ryan Elliott and Danny Barber finished runner-up to the Netherlands in the final.

It was Australia's fifth consecutive World Championships medal in the event.

"For the final, we made a minor change in strategy," Hoffman said.

British track cyclist Matthew Richardson, who defected from Australian cycling at the end of the Paris Games, has been withdrawn from this week's UCI Track World Championships in Shanghai.

"We just tried to have a little gamble, and it almost paid off.

"We were up to the 500-metre mark, so we definitely gave the Dutch a run for their money.

"It's definitely bittersweet to miss out on the [winner's] rainbow bands, but considering last year was a bronze and this year we have silver, I think this team is on the way up."

Australia won a first-round duel against a British team missing Matt Richardson.

He was withdrawn from the British squad earlier in the week over alleged misconduct.

Richardson won three Olympic medals for Australia before switching allegiance to Great Britain after the 2024 Paris Games.

In other results in Shanghai, Australia's Kristina Clonan, Molly McGill and Alessia McCaig finished seventh in the women's team sprint.

ABC/AAP
